notes: All 29 relevant thrower source playbooks were read. -9bQzRv7slI supplies only a Clan Castle recommendation and no tactical steps; WZbB1yebB9A supplies sparse revival and ability commentary rather than a complete deployment sequence.

Support counts distinct videos describing an action or tactical role, including a source's explicitly described alternatives; it does not mean every supporting video uses the selected count, equipment, or identical deployment order. Replays within one video count once.

BMlNYGg37J8 and T9LOFmCucwo share the largest identical complete primary army preset: two videos, not a majority of the 29. This preset supplies the default counts and loadouts. Reserve Log Launcher, Flame Flinger, Siege Barracks, and donated Troop Launcher entries are inventory choices; the executable army keeps one active Log Launcher and does not treat other siege options as troops or Clan Castle payload.

The default order follows the recurrent Duke-first, Throwers-Healers-Warden, opposite hero funnel, siege pattern. 5InNp3cBzCA explicitly starts Throwers immediately after Duke; BMlNYGg37J8 and T9LOFmCucwo describe allowing his funnel to develop. Other videos start Throwers first, open with a Warden walk, or delay Duke. No numerical funnel duration is established.

Citation t values are video timestamps, never battle timers. Battle t=0 means the stated opening. Every after/delay=0 is the required fallback for an unquantified sequence; it is not a measured delay or a claim that the source prescribes simultaneous actions.

group_inside:main approximates 'the Throwers have advanced' before the side heroes and delayed siege. group_inside:walk approximates completion of a Warden walk. inside:Firemite approximates Firemites breaching the base. These predicates do not prove that a compartment has been cleared.

edge:main represents the narrated deployment behind or alongside the Throwers without inventing tile offsets. edge:charge and edge:funnel are scouted flanks, not fixed compass directions. The chosen entry and Log Launcher angle still need to give the intended route toward the Town Hall.

threat:main is the closest available anchor for an indicated dangerous compartment. heavy_fire:Thrower approximates substantial incoming damage; it cannot identify a Rage Tower activation, an Overgrowth expiry, or the precise area that would split the army. The default Skeleton cast uses the same coarse danger trigger for the Monolith. These approximations may make several protective spells eligible together.

One Ice Block is scripted when Duke takes heavy fire. The remaining donated Ice Blocks are held because no numerical repeat interval is stated. No every interval, HP fraction, Town Hall radius, destruction percentage, or cleanup timestamp has been invented. Totem replacement after a previous Totem dies and spell-effect expiry are not expressible by the listed triggers.

Revive is retained as a cited policy instead of a knowingly nonfunctional step: the current executor's unit anchor resolves only living units, so unit:Dragon Duke with dead:Dragon Duke cannot locate his fallen position. The vocabulary provides no corpse anchor. No unrelated edge or living group is substituted for the fallen hero. The two default Revive Spells therefore remain unscripted.

Revive priorities are contested: NrogBoJyRVI allows Duke or King, T9LOFmCucwo and dHij_8HI47w revive Queen late, and XTTBlGH4zXE forbids King/Queen revives and chooses Warden when many Throwers remain or Duke when few remain. No numerical definition of many or few is supplied.

The default rear Ruin Witch uses the selected preset's single remaining witch. BMlNYGg37J8 calls it only 'a witch'; its army identifies Ruin Witch, while other cited sources explicitly name Ruin Witches. The primary script does not invent deployment timing for the remaining Archers, Baby Dragon, Balloons, Super Barbarians, or second Super Wall Breaker.

The default Grand Warden has Life Gem and Rage Gem, with no invented active-ability timing. Early Warden activation belongs to gVNS9seD83w's Heroic Torch variant. XTTBlGH4zXE's endgame Warden policy is not the TH15 Root Rider ability policy in BMlNYGg37J8, which is outside this thrower plan.

The Troop Launcher variant requires replacing army.cc.Log Launcher with Troop Launcher, retaining the selected payload; deploy one siege machine. Its support of four counts the cited open/short-route alternatives, not every video that mentions Troop Launcher.

The late-King variant uses Queen's counterfunnel and immediate ability, then approximates the later King deployment by after:overgrowth with delay 0. 15TbHFSYt84 and XibexH-PFis describe Stick Horse and Angry Jelly for a separate King role; 15TbHFSYt84 also names Giant Gauntlet. Use the corresponding source loadout rather than assuming the default Snake Bracelet pairing has the same role.

The full Zapquake variant uses the Monolith cluster as one explicitly supported target. 0h7c4WKuPB8 and FfvfHeRMDZs prioritize Cake Catapult/Cake-A-Pult, then Revenge Tower, then Monolith, while requiring useful adjacent defenses rather than automatically spending eight spells on an isolated target. No single selected-cluster anchor exists, so other clusters require a scouted target substitution. The two Earthquakes and six Lightnings are separate count-1 casts because the current spell executor casts once per step. Exact spell order is not stated; Earthquakes followed by Lightnings is a serialization with delay 0, not a measured source timing.

The Giant Arrow/Rocket Backpack variant requires Queen with Giant Arrow and Duke with Rocket Backpack, and the source's Earthquake-bearing spell preset. Three Earthquakes follow Xk6Q2cZqvHM; AZTUaqyRtew instead states at least two for level-24 Rocket Backpack, at least three for level 21 against buildings with at least 6000 HP, and uses four in its example. The script's Monolith anchor is one allowed priority target, not a reconstruction of all separate target sections or Builder's Huts.

AZTUaqyRtew fires Giant Arrow before Rocket Backpack; Xk6Q2cZqvHM demonstrates Duke firing first. The Arrow variant follows AZTUaqyRtew's order. The provided vocabulary cannot encode either projectile's drawn alignment or the heroes' landing positions; source advice uses building midpoints/corners and often opposite starting positions. Those aiming decisions remain unresolved by these steps.

The mini-Zapquake variant follows aLOitRlGp8g's Rocket Backpack, two Earthquakes, and three Lightnings. Its Duke loadout is Rocket Backpack/Revenge Deck/Phoenix and it uses that source's army. OWBSVJa-H_E also narrates Rocket Backpack followed by Lightning finishing, but does not narrate its linked Earthquake casts; it is not counted as support for the complete two-Earthquake/three-Lightning variant.

The Warden-walk variant needs the two Furnaces stated in XTTBlGH4zXE and draws the Warden toward the main Throwers. Its simplified counterfunnel follows the cited walk alternatives; XTTBlGH4zXE additionally allocates one Thrower, a Wizard and a Baby Dragon to its opposite opening, while XibexH-PFis's illustrated walk omits Ruin Witches. The selected default army lacks Furnaces, so load the corresponding source preset before this variant.

HJfCl7Ycf6E specifies four to five Furnaces and explicitly uses five. Its Clone variant records only the first cast: Clone totals, spacing, overlapping centers toward the core, and completion of the chain are not numerically specified. after:first_clone/delay=0 is only the permitted sequence fallback for the later Thrower phase, not a complete executable Clone chain. Furnace and Clone inventory, optional Rage, Healer deployment, and Stun Blaster/Fire Heart Duke loadout must come from that source; unknown counts are not filled in.

The Spirit Walk variant uses gVNS9seD83w's Duke with Fire Heart/Monolith Arrow/Spirit Fox, Warden with Heroic Torch/Rage Gem/Diggy, and its Invisibility-bearing army. That source assigns Frosty to King and Greedy Raven to Queen, avoiding the default King's Spirit Fox assignment. The source says cast at timer readings ending in six and prioritize covering Spirit Fox; the timer origin is not identified. Only the first Invisibility is represented, using inside:Dragon Duke as the closest ongoing-charge trigger. No repeat cadence is invented.

The Yeti variant follows zSh-YQVhKT8: eight Throwers, two Ice Golems, and Yetis whose total is unstated. Its all count means the Yetis in that source army, not a newly inferred quantity. Load a source-compatible army before selecting it. -9bQzRv7slI adds only Super Yeti 1/Ice Golem 1 with donated Earthquake 2/Rage 1; it does not establish the main Yeti count or support an attack sequence.

The Skeleton-package variant uses dxLogWcc0VU's eight Skeleton Spells, one Overgrowth and one Poison, with two donated Revives. It replaces Totem actions with an initial front distraction and a later Monolith distraction; the retained Monolith Skeleton step is another available cast. Other Skeletons remain discretionary because no interval is stated. The source explicitly saves a couple for the back end and suggests Eternal Tome instead of Life Gem for a committed Town Hall entry.

6UjxhDyQkyI uses eleven Throwers, ten Healers and three Super Wall Breakers, with five Healers on each flank and central heroes plus Log Launcher. It says split Throwers half and half without specifying the unequal division of eleven, and does not identify all central heroes. Its variant intentionally has no executable replacement steps; assigning numeric Thrower partitions or hero identities would invent information.

Other stated Thrower/Healer totals: 11/5 in 3KPlpZZeWsg and XTTBlGH4zXE; 8/5 in AZTUaqyRtew, WZbB1yebB9A and hiT9weAx9pQ; 9/5 in 5InNp3cBzCA, eeDapoJl4d8 and ufdEws4wP9c; 10/5 in NrogBoJyRVI and aRUj8A45u4A; 10/4 in C0mxv9JyBAk; 10/6 in aLOitRlGp8g; 12/5 in FfvfHeRMDZs, OWBSVJa-H_E, dHij_8HI47w, dxLogWcc0VU and gVNS9seD83w. 15TbHFSYt84 states nine Throwers and three Ruin Witches, XibexH-PFis states nine Throwers with incomplete support totals, and zSh-YQVhKT8 states eight Throwers with an unspecified Yeti/Healer total. 0h7c4WKuPB8, HJfCl7Ycf6E, Xk6Q2cZqvHM, uzgXTc3seHY and wFK5O0nLJEw do not establish complete Thrower/Healer counts.

Other main support compositions differ materially: C0mxv9JyBAk and WZbB1yebB9A have four Ruin Witches; 15TbHFSYt84 has three; FfvfHeRMDZs, NrogBoJyRVI, aLOitRlGp8g, dxLogWcc0VU, eeDapoJl4d8, gVNS9seD83w, hiT9weAx9pQ, ufdEws4wP9c and wFK5O0nLJEw have two; aRUj8A45u4A has one. NrogBoJyRVI adds two Druids; 5InNp3cBzCA, OWBSVJa-H_E, aRUj8A45u4A and hiT9weAx9pQ list one. AZTUaqyRtew and XTTBlGH4zXE list two Furnaces, eeDapoJl4d8 one, and the Firemite Clone opening uses five. 0h7c4WKuPB8's narration adds one or two Electro Titans. These are source alternatives, not additions to the default army.

Other spell packages include: FfvfHeRMDZs's Totem 1/Ice Block 2/Earthquake 2/Lightning 6; NrogBoJyRVI's Totem 2/Ice Block 2/Revive 2/Overgrowth 1/Poison 1; C0mxv9JyBAk's Totem 3/Ice Block 2/Revive 2/Overgrowth 1; WZbB1yebB9A's Revive 3/Poison 1/Totem 2/Overgrowth 1; XTTBlGH4zXE's Totem 6/Poison 1/Overgrowth 1/Skeleton 1/Freeze 1; aLOitRlGp8g's Ice Block 1/Poison 1/Earthquake 2/Lightning 3/Revive 2; hiT9weAx9pQ's Totem 2/Freeze 2/Poison 1/Overgrowth 1/Revive 2. These replace the default package rather than supplementing it.

Further spell alternatives: 5InNp3cBzCA lists Totem 3/Freeze 1/Ice Block 3/Revive 2 with donated Overgrowth 1/Poison 1; aRUj8A45u4A lists Invisibility 1/Revive 2/Ice Block 2/Overgrowth 1/Skeleton 1/Poison 1 with donated Freeze 1/Totem 2; ufdEws4wP9c lists Totem 3/Skeleton 1/Freeze 1/Ice Block 3/Invisibility 1/Overgrowth 1 with donated Revive 1/Poison 1. dHij_8HI47w lists Totem 3/Freeze 2/Poison 1/Invisibility 1/Skeleton 1/Overgrowth 1/Ice Block 1 with donated Revive 2.

Rocket and charge spell alternatives: AZTUaqyRtew lists Earthquake 4/Totem 3/Rage 2 with donated Revive 1/Totem 1; OWBSVJa-H_E's Backpack preset lists Totem 3/Lightning 3/Freeze 2/Poison 1/Earthquake 2 with donated Overgrowth 1/Revive 1, and its Revenge Deck preset is the alternative later listed in that extraction; eeDapoJl4d8 lists Earthquake 3/Totem 3/Overgrowth 1/Freeze 1/Poison 1/Invisibility 1 with donated Recall 1/Revive 1; gVNS9seD83w lists Revive 1/Poison 1/Totem 4/Invisibility 4 with donated Angry 1/Freeze 1/Overgrowth 1. Sources with partial spell inventories are not completed by borrowing quantities from other videos.

Other Clan Castle payloads include three Ice Golems and two Balloons with donated Revive 2 in FfvfHeRMDZs, aLOitRlGp8g and dxLogWcc0VU; NrogBoJyRVI uses the same payload and Revive count. 5InNp3cBzCA instead lists Ice Golem 1/Balloon 1/Super Valkyrie 1/Giant 2; AZTUaqyRtew lists Yeti 1/Root Rider 1/Rocket Balloon 1/Minion 2; XTTBlGH4zXE and gVNS9seD83w list Super Valkyrie 1/Super Yeti 1. These are alternative payloads, not combined donations.

eeDapoJl4d8's further Recall branch picks up Queen after her initial funnel and redeploys her to create a second funnel; one replay recalls Duke too. Its Giant Arrow/Healer Puppet Queen, Rocket Backpack/Fire Heart Duke and donated Recall 1 belong to that source's army. No numerical recall trigger, exact redeployment location, or complete initial deployment is stated, so the branch is recorded without invented executable placements.

Town Hall entry preferences conflict: 3KPlpZZeWsg generally favors the far side and dHij_8HI47w accepts leaving Town Hall late; 15TbHFSYt84, 0h7c4WKuPB8 and aLOitRlGp8g favor earlier Town Hall access when practical. Spring Trap bait and Firespitter/Sweeper orientation can reverse a nominal Monolith or Town Hall preference.

Retain ambiguous labels such as logger, candle, cake, long shot and hero hunter where the extraction does not establish their in-game identity. The defensive logger is not the attacking Log Launcher. Do not convert unclear Recall/Revive captions in 0h7c4WKuPB8 into an extra recall sequence. Defensive-base Clan Castle descriptions in 15TbHFSYt84, XibexH-PFis and zSh-YQVhKT8 are not attacking reinforcement evidence.
